messages.subject: Different probability results when running the model multiple times
parts:
Hi all, I was wondering if someone could provide some further clarification as to why our INLA model may be giving different results every time that we run our code.

I was reading about others having this similar problem here, but this question regarded different results on different computers. I am currently running the model multiple times on the same code. An example in difference of probabilities I am receiving is: 0.00430474561287514 vs. 0.0116855131964157

The code we used is below. Thanks in advance for any clarification!:

#===================================================================================
# IVb. Set up data in INLA format
#===================================================================================

# create datasets of observations 
dataforfit <- df[which(df$outcome == 1 | df$outcome == 0),]
datapred <- df[which(df$insptime == 4),]

# print out number of observations of each timestep
print(paste0("Number of observations from time step 1: ", length(which(dataforfit$insptime == 1))))
print(paste0("Number of observations from time step 2: ", length(which(dataforfit$insptime == 2))))
print(paste0("Number of observations from time step 3: ", length(which(dataforfit$insptime == 3))))
print(paste0("Number of observations from time step 4: ", length(which(dataforfit$insptime == 4))))

# print out sizes of dataforfit and datapred
print(paste0("Size of dataforfit: ", nrow(dataforfit)))
print(paste0("Size of datapred: ", nrow(datapred)))

# define time dimension
k <- length(unique(df$insptime))

# define two coordinate matrices
coords1<- cbind(dataforfit$LONGITUDEscale, dataforfit$LATITUDEscale)
coords <- cbind(datapred$LONGITUDEscale, datapred$LATITUDEscale)

# create mesh
mesh1 <- inla.mesh.2d(coords1, max.edge=c(50*S,50*S), cutoff=0.2)

# create two A matrices
A.est <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=mesh1,
                          loc=coords1,
                          group=dataforfit$insptime,n.group=k)

A.prd <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=mesh1, loc=coords, group=datapred$insptime)

# create SPDE object of Matern covariance matrix
spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh1, 
                          alpha=2,
                          theta.prior.mean=c(8,-5),
                          theta.prior.prec=c(0.1,0.1))

# create mesh index
mesh.index <- inla.spde.make.index(name='spatial', 
                                   n.spde=spde$n.spde,n.group=k)

# create stack object for data for fit
stack.est =
  inla.stack(data=list(y=dataforfit$outcome),
             A=list(A.est,1),
             effects=
               list(c(mesh.index,list(Intercept=1)),
                    list(
                      not_sprayed=dataforfit$not_sprayed)),
             tag="est")

# create stack object for data for prediction
stack.pred =
  inla.stack(data=list(y=datapred$outcome),
             A=list(A.prd,1),
             effects=
               list(c(mesh.index,list(Intercept=1)),
                    list(
                      not_sprayed=datapred$not_sprayed)),
             tag="pred")

# combine stack objects  
stack = inla.stack(stack.est, stack.pred)

# formula to input into INLA
formula <- y ~ -1 + Intercept + not_sprayed + f(spatial, 
                                                model=spde, 
                                                group=spatial.group, 
                                                control.group=list(model='ar1', 
                                                                   hyper=list(theta=list(prior='pccor1', param=c(0, 0.9)))))

#===================================================================================
# IVc. Run INLA model
#===================================================================================

# priors are set by control.fixed
result <- inla(formula,
               data = inla.stack.data(stack, spde=spde),
               family = c("binomial"),verbose=TRUE,
               #control.predictor = list(A=inla.stack.A(stack), compute=TRUE,link=1)  # Produces estimates
               control.predictor = list(A=inla.stack.A(stack), compute=TRUE,link=1)
               ,control.inla = list(reordering = "metis")
               ,control.fixed = list(mean = list(Intercept=-6.9, not_sprayed=1.17), # Prior means
                                     prec = list(Intercept=0.1, not_sprayed=0.1))  #Prior standard deviations
               #,num.threads=4  # uses 4 cores may be helpful
)

# runs a second inla model starting at the median of the first one
result <- inla.rerun(result)  

result.f <- inla.spde2.result(result, "spatial", spde, do.transf=TRUE)

parts:
You’re not running the model twice, you are running it more steps (rerun is similar to continuing the optimisation iterations) which makes a difference for models with illdefined logposterior maximum. With a binomial likelihood and and a very large prior standard deviations for the SPDE parameters it’s likely your posterior is problematic. (~3 is quite large when the field is used on the log-scale. How did you choose the spde prior settings? They look very strange! You should consider using the inla.spde2.pcmatern() model instead.)

What is the verbose output? I suspect your field parameter estimates diverge.

Finn

parts:
Hi,

multithreading can also lead to different results due to order of
operations (but usually not as large as the one you quoted; however,
if the model is ill-defined, I'd expect those differences to be more
noticeable than for well-defined models).

spde2.matern and spde2.pcmatern differ in the type of prior
distributions used for the parameters (see the help texts). The spde
parameters used by the pcmatern version (range and std.dev.) is also
easier to interpret than the default spde2.matern parameterisation
(tau and kappa).
Have you read the "read this first" spde tutorial document on
r-inla.org? It gives a suggested way of setting the parameterisation
and priors for the regular spde2.matern model, which is similar in
spirit to what you can specify directly with the spde2.pcmatern model.

For verbose output, including a trace of the optimisation:
... <- inla(..., verbose=TRUE)

Finn
